## What you did
- Root-caused the flaky `test_acs_rejects_expired_assertion` (a 2.1 s sleep against a 3 s clock skew): froze time with freezegun, converted the two other sleeping tests the same way, and the ACS file now passes 50/50 on repeat, ~2 s faster [1].
- Cleared `ruff` 0.8 and the two mypy errors it hid in `kestrel/auth` — a missing Issuer/Subject is now a 401 instead of a 500 — and split the 900-line `saml_utils.py` into `saml/{assertions,metadata,bindings}.py` behind a shim, full suite green [1].

## What changed
- Maya approved and merged #418: signature verification goes out with tonight's staging deploy, so it will be on staging ahead of Fernhill IT's end-to-end SSO walkthrough Thursday 10am NY on their Okta tenant (Priya runs the demo, you're on the call) [3][1].
- Tom requested changes on #423: he can't read the real changes inside a 1,900-line diff, wants the module move and the lint fixes in two separate PRs, and says he'll approve both today [4].

## What is still open
- #423 to split in two before Tom's review, keeping #418 untouched [4][1].
- The replay cache is still process-local, so a replay can hit another pod; moving it to Redis (keyed by tenant + assertion ID, TTL = NotOnOrAfter + skew, client already in `kestrel/cache.py`) is the work you lined up for today [1].
- A non-blocking nit from Maya on the #418 error message wording [3].
